newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan police break up banned student march.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan police break up banned student march.

text.p: Venezuelan riot police fired tear gas and plastic bullets to break up a banned student protest on Wednesday over low teachers' pay and insufficient funding for universities.
"Our orders were to stop the march at all costs," a police spokesman said outside Caracas's Central University where the 1,500-strong protest was to have taken place.
Witnesses said two people were hurt. About 40 students, their faces covered with shirts, joined the stalled march throwing rocks and homemade explosives at police, they added.
Local radio reports said police also stopped busloads of students on the outskirts of the capital from joining what was to have been a national protest.
The Caracas town council banned the march on the grounds that the organisers did not provide adequate plans to protect the peace and private property.
Venezuelan university teachers are in the third week of strikes to demand a 125 percent pay rise. The government has stuck firm to a 50 percent offer.
